newsitem.title: USA: Genovese crime family extorted money from festival.
newsitem.headline: Genovese crime family extorted money from festival.

text.p: Six members of the powerful Genovese crime family pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in New York Monday to extorting money from vendors at New York's most popular street festival.

The defendants made a plea bargain in a case that also involved charges of murder and racketeering. It was the broadest racketeering indictment ever brought against the nation's most influential mafia group, prosecutors said.
The six include Liborio "Barney" Bellomo, 40, the alleged acting boss. He faces 10 years in prison when sentenced June 2 by U.S. District Judge Lewis Kaplan.
Michael Generoso, 79, the alleged acting underboss, faces up to five years in prison.
The case stems from allegations the defendants fraudulently controlled the annual Feast of San Gennaro, New York City's most popular street festival.

"With these pleas, there is certainty that one of the leaders of one of the largest and most powerful organised crime groups in the country will go to jail for 10 years without the possibility of parole," Mary Jo White, the U.S. Attorney, said.

The 11-day event, held in Manhattan's Little Italy, is supposedly run by a non-profit, tax-exempt group called the Society Saint Gennaro Naples & Suburbs that raises money for churches and charities. But prosecutors alleged the defendants ran the festival in 1993 and 1994, taking most of the rent paid by vendors.
The city operated the festival in 1996 for the first time and generated $150,000 for charity.
The indictment alleged that Bellomo and Generoso participated in murders, extortion and other crimes that generated at least $20 million in illegal profits.
The four others face a maximum of 25 years in prison.
According to the plea agreement, the defendants also face substantial fines. They have also agreed to forfeit an additional $3 million to the government.
Three other defendants in the case go on trial Feb. 24.
Federal authorities said the Genovese family was the most powerful and diversified in the United States.
